title: City man died being held in police custody
article: A Sarnia man who died after being arrested on Highway 402 was being taken for a mental-health assessment when he became unresponsive and an OPP officer called for an ambulance, a coroner's inquest heard Tuesday.
Paul Thomas Horan, 43, died in the early morning of Sept. 24, 2010 at Bluewater Health's Charlotte Eleanor Englehart Hospital in Petrolia.
He was arrested hours earlier for failing to stop for police, because the vehicle he was driving had invalid licence plates.
The five-member coroner's jury was told by presiding coroner Dr. Thomas Wilson they had to determine how Horan died, and possibly make recommendations to prevent similar deaths.
The inquest's purpose is not to find blame for Horan's death or free anyone of blame, coroner's counsel Randy Evans said during his opening remarks to jurors.
A letter from the Horan family read to the jurors stated Horan was a hard worker, a prankster and a hopeless romantic who won't get to live his dream of becoming a husband and father.
Evans said evidence is expected to show Horan died from an overdose of methadone and an anti-depressant medication.
The first witness was a Sarnia police officer who testified he dealt with Horan on Dec. 18, 2009, when Horan said he'd taken 150 prescription pills and had been depressed.

A Dec. 19, 2009 doctor's report filed with the inquest stated Horan was treated for an overdose, but denied any suicidal intention and did not appear depressed. Horan told the doctor he was frustrated about being evicted from his residence because a roommate failed to pay the rent.

On the evening of Sept. 23, 2010, Horan was driving a car eastbound on Highway 402 near Forest Road when an OPP officer checked the licence plate. The plate was expired and didn't belong on the car being driven by Horan.
The officer pursued the car for a short distance with the lights and siren activated. Horan was partially deaf.
After he stopped, Horan was arrested, handcuffed and placed in the back of the cruiser because he hadn't immediately stopped, although he was driving at just 90 kilometres per hour.
During the pursuit, the OPP officer saw something tossed from the driver's window, which proved to be an empty prescription pill bottle.

A search of the car found three empty methadone bottles. Horan was taking the prescription methadone to deal with an oxycodone addiction that developed from painkillers being prescribed for a back injury.
There was also a large jug of a cleaning solution that appeared to have been spilt in on the passenger-side floor.
A pellet gun was found under the driver's seat.
Horan said he had the gun so the police would be forced to shoot him if he was stopped.
Horan's answer prompted OPP Const. Peter Tishler to head for Bluewater Health in Sarnia so Horan's mental health could be assessed.
As Tishler headed for Sarnia, he was told about the previous overdose.
"Something was not sitting right with me . . . I had in my mind he had been drinking the cleaning solution," said Tishler.
Tishler stopped driving to check Horan. Horan said nothing and his eyes were rolling back in his head and Tishler called for an ambulance.
Another officer who was following Tishler helped him remove Horan from the cruiser, remove the handcuffs and put him on the ground.
Horan was breathing, but the officers were prepared to start cardio-pulmonary resuscitation.
Paramedics found Horan's heart rate was elevated but he was still breathing as they headed for Bluewater Health in Petrolia.
The inquest, which continues Wednesday, is expected to last into next week.
